encoding.note: os.path.exists(...) is a runtime filesystem probe with no static structure, so it is abstracted to a single boolean atom `exists`. The branch predicate is then the trivial negation Not(exists). z3 decides it exhaustively over both atom assignments. This mirrors the ExpressionEvaluator unary(not) op only; the underlying atom is opaque (a stat() syscall), not an expression z3 can decompose.

true_examples.source: z3-model + on-disk verification (file does NOT exist -> printExit branch taken)

false_examples.source: z3-model + on-disk verification (file created with ProblemType: {} -> branch NOT taken, proceeds to LibraryIO.read)

pure_helper:
def metadata_missing(exists: bool) -> bool:
    # True when metadata.yaml is absent (the printExit branch is taken).
    # `exists` abstracts os.path.exists(metaDataFilePath); the predicate logic is the bare negation.
    return not exists

crosshair.caveat: absence of a counterexample is NOT a proof; for a bool->bool negation it is merely consistent with correctness.

runtime_note: The predicate LOGIC (a negated boolean atom) is fully static and z3 decides both branches sat. But the atom is os.path.exists(metaDataFilePath), a live filesystem stat() -- NOT something z3 can solve internally; it is abstracted. UNLIKE a pure OS probe such as os.name, this atom IS reachable from public input: metaDataFilePath = os.path.join(libraryDir(libraryRootPath, archs or []), 'metadata.yaml'), so a caller controls the branch entirely via the libraryRootPath / archs arguments. Pointing CreateBenchmarkClientParametersForSizes at a library dir WITHOUT metadata.yaml drives the True branch (printExit 'meta data file ... does not exist'); a dir WITH metadata.yaml drives the False branch (read the file -> ProblemType). Note this whole else-block only runs when problemTypeDict is falsy. Both seeded paths were materialized on the char-test host and os.path.exists returned False/True respectively, matching the z3 models. classification=runtime-dependent because the taken branch is determined by filesystem state at call time, not by a solver over symbolic inputs.
